titel: Tiny print in your slicer? Fix it in Blender 🔍 #blender #3dprinting

eind.zin: A new Blender tip for 3D printing every week.

printzin: Measured in Blender, not print tested by us yet.

scenes.tekst: Is your print tiny in the slicer? Check this in Blender.
scenes.label: QUICK TIP

scenes.tekst: Press N. Blender says this tag is 60 mm wide.
scenes.uitspraak: Press N. Blender says this tag is sixty millimeters wide.
scenes.label: STEP 1

scenes.tekst: But Unit Scale is 1, so inside the file it is 0.06.
scenes.uitspraak: But Unit Scale is one, so inside the file it is zero point zero six.
scenes.label: WHY

scenes.tekst: An STL file has no unit. Most slicers read that as 0.06 mm.
scenes.uitspraak: An STL file has no unit. Most slicers read that as zero point zero six millimeters.
scenes.label: WHY

scenes.tekst: Set Scale to 1000, then click Export STL.
scenes.uitspraak: Set Scale to one thousand, then click Export S T L.
scenes.label: STEP 3

scenes.tekst: Now the file says 60 mm, the same as in Blender.
scenes.uitspraak: Now the file says sixty millimeters, the same as in Blender.
scenes.label: RESULT

scenes.tekst: Measured in Blender, not print tested by us yet. Save this for your next export.
scenes.label: HONEST
